bull_bear.body: Buybacks remain preferred option over dividends (Dividend INR 1/share proposed); ESOP trust bought INR 250Cr shares from market in FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Proposed NPRM on offshore call restrictions (US telcos/cable); Regulatory stringency in BFSI; AI-driven deflation in contract values; High attrition (21%); FX hedging at INR 89 limits upside in FY27.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and disciplined; emphasizing 'top quartile' growth ambition; cautious on fashion/retail but optimistic on high-tech and FCC; transparent about AI deflationary pressures but framing them as opportunities for wallet share gain.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Shift to outcome-based pricing in AI projects (e.g., 50% cost reduction in KYC refresh) rather than pure FTE models; Internal adoption of 'Roboworx/Cogniflows' by 3,000+ employees driving productivity before client billing; Subcon expense spike was purely accounting reclassification, not operational shift.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend of INR 1 proposed for FY27.
- Cash and Cash Equivalents were INR 12,589 mm at Q1 FY27 against INR 12,810 mm at FY26; per share, cash was INR 137 at Q1 FY27 versus current book value per share of INR 300. Note the deck flags that effective Q4FY25 deposits of more than 12 months are included in this figure.
- Current Book Value per share has risen on the deck's series from INR 179 (FY23) to INR 300 (Q1 FY27), with the deck noting historical numbers were changed due to the Bonus issued in Q4 FY26.
- Hedging is a deliberate treasury policy rather than opportunistic: total outstanding hedges of $273.6 mm at an average INR 93.41/$, 100% forwards, laddered out to FY29 Q1 (Total FY27 $156.20 mm at 91.16; Total FY28 $112.00 mm at 96.20; Total FY29 $5.40 mm at 100.85).
- The deck cites a 17.5% 4-Year Revenue CAGR from FY22 to FY26.

business.body:
- Described as "a global leader in AI-powered analytics, digital operations, automation, and business process management", partnering with Fortune 500 enterprises across financial services, telecom, media & entertainment, luxury, retail & fashion, and manufacturing.
- Delivery footprint spans 17 countries with around 22,500 employees, serving clients across the Americas, APAC and EMEA from global delivery centres.
- Client base is broad rather than concentrated in one vertical: Q1'FY27 revenue by industry is BFSI 37.6%, CMT 26.2%, HiTech and M&D 16.3%, Fashion & Luxury and Retail 8.2%, Emerging 11.7%.
- Top 10 client contribution was 60% in FY27 Q1, versus 63% in FY26 Q1 and 62% in FY25 Q1 — i.e. gradually declining concentration on the deck's own series.
- Geographic concentration in FY27 Q1: North America 78%, Europe 16%, ROW 6%; currency contribution USD 87%, EURO 8%, GBP 3%, Others 2%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Bonus issue] The deck states "Changes in historical numbers due to Bonus issued in Q4 FY26", so per-share history on these slides is restated.
- [Accounting change] "*Effective Q4FY25 we have included Deposits more than 12 months" in the Cash and Cash Equivalents series, so FY25 onward is not comparable with FY23/FY24 on that line.
- [FX] Quarter-exit rates disclosed: USD/INR FY27 Q1 exit 94.56 vs FY26 Q4 exit 93.78; EUR/INR 108.01 vs 108.09; GBP/INR 125.47 vs 123.84. The deck says revaluation income decreased due to lower INR depreciation against USD in Q1.
- [Definitions] The deck defines EBIT as including other income and excluding rental interest under IND AS116, and states EBITDA and EBIT percentages are computed on Total Revenue — so its margin labels are not directly comparable with an operating-revenue basis.

deepdive.thesis: eClerx delivered record FY26 results with 17.9% USD revenue growth and 132 bps margin expansion, driven by a $90M analytics book and first large-scale Agentic AI wins, positioning it for top-quartile growth in FY27 despite macro headwinds. The strategic pivot to outcome-based AI services and diversification beyond BFSI reduces concentration risk while enhancing operating leverage.

open.item: eClerx is reorienting key areas of its BFSI business around data and AI, with targeted investments in client-facing field teams, leadership, India-based technology and AI capabilities, product development, and employee enablement.

eClerx is reorienting key BFSI business areas around data and AI, with targeted investment in client-facing field teams, leadership, India-based technology and AI capabilities, product development and employee enablement.
eClerx expects continued momentum for QA360, its AI-powered Quality Intelligence platform, with multiple new client deployments planned.

eClerx expects continued investment in its global delivery network, further strengthening strategic delivery locations such as Manila, Cairo and Lima to support increasing client demand and enhance operational resilience.
eClerx expects the growth momentum in its Emerging Business vertical (led by Finance and Accounting/FAO services) to carry forward into FY27.
Company intends to maintain its historical dividend payout ratio going forward and is exploring efficient methods to achieve the same.
Financial Crime and Compliance remains a key strategic focus area, with continued investment in solutioning, product capabilities and AI-enabled functionality driving a growing pipeline.

Focus on identifying and expanding strategic accounts and driving cross-sell across the High-Tech, Manufacturing & Distribution, Fashion & Luxury, Retail and Consumer Goods vertical, including new client acquisition in Marketing Intelligence and Data Operations and expansion of Digital Marketing offerings.

Following the launch of NOC capabilities, eClerx will continue investing in technology-led operational services, including infrastructure support and adjacent technical operations, broadening its portfolio beyond traditional customer operations.

risks.note: Large clients possess greater bargaining power, which can result in pricing concessions, extended payment terms, or demands for additional scope at no incremental cost, compressing margins over time; deterioration, delayed payments, insolvency, or a change in control/strategy at a top client (e.g. insourcing or vendor consolidation) can lead to abrupt, largely uncontrollable loss of business.

The Company earned 87% of its revenue in US Dollars, 9% in Euros, and 4% in Sterling and other currencies, so exchange rate fluctuations can negatively impact financial performance; hedging strategies are used but do not eliminate the exposure.

The industry is highly competitive and evolving rapidly, with changing client expectations, new entrants, technology disruption and pricing pressure; low barriers to entry in certain segments allow well-funded technology-first players to disrupt traditional service models, particularly areas susceptible to automation or platform-based delivery.

Legislation in some client countries may restrict outsourcing of work to overseas entities like eClerx, which could hamper growth in major markets; withdrawal or material alteration of export/tax incentives, and evolving regulation around AI, cybersecurity, sanctions, employment and data protection, could increase compliance obligations, operational complexity and costs.

Rapid advances in automation, AI and digital tools are reshaping client expectations and service delivery models; competitors that adopt new technologies faster, or clients that build in-house automation, could reduce demand for traditional service offerings and erode eClerx's competitive positioning if it does not keep pace with innovation.

The business relies extensively on IT systems and handles significant volumes of confidential client data; a breach (hacking, phishing, malware, insider threat, ransomware or DoS attack) could cause unauthorized data access/theft, breach client confidentiality agreements, trigger regulatory penalties and SLA/contractual liability, and reliance on third-party vendors/cloud providers adds exposure outside direct control.
risks.risk: Cyber security incident / cyber attack risk

risks.note: The business is critically dependent on the quality, expertise and commitment of its workforce; inability to attract, develop, retain and motivate key talent could adversely affect service delivery quality, client expectations and long-term growth objectives.

Past or future acquisitions may pose financial, technological, operational and people integration risks; challenges integrating acquired businesses, personnel, technology platforms, internal controls and organizational cultures could divert management attention, disrupt ongoing business, increase costs, and expose the Company to cyber and information security risks.
